title: ExeGPT: Constraint-Aware Resource Scheduling for LLM Inference
problem: LLM inference requires simultaneous optimization of throughput and latency, requiring effective resource allocation and configuration decisions. Current systems lack mechanisms to dynamically adapt batch sizes and tensor parallelism based on latency constraints and sequence length distributions.
motivation: LLM inference is a critical bottleneck in production systems, and meeting latency Service Level Objectives while maximizing utilization is essential for cost-effective deployment.
method: ExeGPT develops an optimal execution scheduler that analyzes input/output sequence length distributions to determine ideal batch sizes and partial tensor parallelism configurations. It implements two scheduling strategies: Round-Robin Allocation for uniform workloads and Workload-Aware Allocation for heterogeneous NLP workloads, dynamically adapting execution plans to satisfy latency constraints.
key_novelty: Constraint-aware scheduling that jointly optimizes batch size and partial tensor parallelism to maximize throughput while guaranteeing latency bounds.
contributions: Optimal execution scheduling framework for latency-constrained LLM inference
Resource allocation methodology leveraging sequence length distributions
Round-Robin and Workload-Aware scheduling strategies for different workload patterns
Dynamic configuration of batch sizes and partial tensor parallelism
